reason: The plan is safe and sensible. After a fully missed week, the draft repeats the last block instead of moving on. Three walk-runs total about 7 km, which matches her recent 6.8–7.3 km weeks. The sessions build gently from 6x to 8x 2 min run / 1 min walk, with easy heart-rate caps and rest days between, and it keeps her Mon/Wed/Sat routine and dog walks. One missed week with 'all good' isn't a real return from a break, so repeating the load doesn't rush her. Each day is clear enough to run. It loses a point for being generic and mechanical. It never asks why the week was missed, which matters most for keeping a new runner consistent. It doesn't respond to her excitement. It doesn't link the plan to the 15 November 5K goal, about 7 weeks away. The line 'four rest days were kept, so nothing was overrun' is filler and reads oddly to a beginner.
